## Highlights

- **0025 — MCP elicitation persistence:** forward reviewed `session` / `always`
  offers through ACP `_x.ai/mcp/elicit`, and return an accepted selection as MCP
  `_meta.persist`. Unoffered selections cancel. Allow once and native TUI consent
  preserve their one-shot behavior. The native Computer Use receiver owns grants.
- **0026 — Computer Use turn-end cleanup:** Grok's native Session actor awaits
  hidden `cua_repl.turn_ended` before terminal ACP responses on completion,
  failure, cancellation, and session close. Calls and cleanup carry matching turn
  identity. On macOS, a trusted wrapper delegates the installed Sky service and
  sends its native turn-ended request. Successful cleanup preserves MCP and REPL
  state. Missing cleanup blocks tool admission; errors or the three-second
  deadline disable the connection.
- The suggested install profile now defaults both memory systems off when the
  corresponding keys are absent. Explicit user choices remain respected.
- Simplify the new patch application tests, run their contract checks in CI, and
  keep the patch inventory table intact.

## Verification and current limits

GrokGod v1.0.53 packages Grok Build **1.0.45**, pinned at
`2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8`, with patches 0001–0026.

Focused native tests, sequential full-stack application checks, and the Mac
source build were verified during implementation. Direct native probes confirmed
ended-turn control rejection with surviving REPL bindings. **Full Clock-through-ACP
completion, real cancellation, next-turn reuse, and visible overlay disappearance
remain pending.** The native actor test run required temporary repairs to existing
test fixtures; those repairs are not part of the distributed patches.

Persist transport support does not establish native grant lifetime or Always
persistence after restart. A `session` token alone does not promise Grok
conversation scope; the native receiver defines that lifetime.

The macOS bridge depends on the installed private Sky IPC contract. Windows and
Linux use the hidden notification and have no live Computer Use acceptance
evidence. No idle timer interrupts an active turn, and cleanup is not guaranteed
after SIGKILL or OS failure. A failed connection does not prove overlay release.
